subject: Proposal: control-plane access clauses and keystore responsibilities for Private Deployments
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@medihub.com>, Olivia Grant <olivia.grant@medihub.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 04 Oct 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private deployment: control-plane & keystore clause proposal

Hi Sam / Olivia,

Following our call this morning, attaching a short note on the clauses we think will resolve the open items in your legal team's redlines. High-level proposal:

- Customer retains control of CMKs (BYOK) and Redwood will only operate the control plane for orchestration; no keys are exported to Redwood-controlled KMS.
- Operator access: Redwood engineers will have ephemeral access for emergency diagnostics but only via documented break-glass with audit logs and MFA; ask is to keep the language to an operational SLA-style annex rather than a blanket "operator access" right in the DPA.
- Cross-border transfers: restrict logs/telemetry that contain customer data to US regions unless explicitly consented.

I've uploaded the DPA redlines (DPA_redlines_v3.pdf) and a keystore responsibilities matrix (keystore_control_matrix.xlsx) that maps responsibilities we propose. Can you review and flag any remaining legal/IT security concerns? Suggest a follow-up call Wednesday if helpful.

Thanks,
Diego
Diego Fernandez
Director, Solutions Legal Ops
Redwood Inference

Attachments: DPA_redlines_v3.pdf (PDF, 35KB); keystore_control_matrix.xlsx (Excel, 12KB)

From: Sam Patel <sam.patel@medihub.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: Olivia Grant <olivia.grant@medihub.com>
Date: Mon, 04 Oct 2027 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment: control-plane & keystore clause proposal

Diego,

Thanks for the snapshot and matrix — helpful. Two immediate asks from our side after an initial pass: 

1) Can you confirm whether any control-plane telemetry (traces, crash dumps) will ever include plaintext customer prompts or model outputs? Our security policy requires those be redacted or routed to customer-controlled storage.

2) The emergency break-glass language: we need a maximum duration for ephemeral access (e.g. 4 hours) and an approval workflow that involves our security on-call and a legal notice.

We want to avoid any interpretation that Redwood could access model payloads for troubleshooting without customer consent.

If you can respond to the two bullets above and send a suggested redline for the operator access annex, we can prep the legal side. Happy to take the Wednesday slot if you propose a time.

Sam
Sam Patel
Head of IT Security, MediHub Health

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 05 Oct 2027 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Private deployment: control-plane & keystore clause proposal

Diego / Karthik —

Looping in a draft operator-access annex that addresses Sam's points. Key items in the draft (attached to this thread as an excerpt):
- Ephemeral access limited to 4 hours by default; extensions require documented approval from customer security and Redwood legal.
- No plaintext customer prompts or responses may be included in telemetry stored in Redwood systems; if raw payloads are captured for debugging, they must be pushed to customer-provided storage (customer-controlled bucket) and purged from Redwood systems within 24 hours.
- Auditability: every break-glass event triggers an immutable audit record (who, why, timestamp, duration) and an automated notification to customer security.
- Proof-of-compliance: Redwood will provide sample audit logs and a weekly summary during the onboarding window and upon request for the first 90 days.

I propose we accept these additions and fold them into DPA_redlines_v3.pdf and re-issue — I'll make the change unless you object.

Irene
Irene Choi
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Date: Wed, 06 Oct 2027 17:45:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Private deployment: control-plane & keystore clause proposal

Sam / Olivia —

Thanks for the quick review and for the clear asks. We updated the DPA redlines and attached the operator-access annex as a separate exhibit. Summary of changes:

- Telemetry: By default, control-plane telemetry will strip or tokenise any model input/output. If a customer requests raw payloads for debugging, Redwood will transfer those payloads directly into customer-provided storage (S3/GCS bucket) and not persist plaintext in Redwood systems beyond 24 hours.
- Break-glass: Ephemeral access limited to 4 hours. Extension requires explicit written approval from MediHub Security + Redwood Legal; all access is authenticated, logged, and triggers immediate notification to MediHub.
- Audit samples: included a sample audit log export (separate CSV) plus a one-page onboarding checklist documenting how mediation/approval will work.

Next steps: 
1) Please confirm the proposed wording by end of Friday 10/08 so we can freeze the DPA and move it to DocuSign.
2) If you want a short alignment call, suggest Thursday 10/07 10:00am PT — otherwise we can do an e-signature path.

I've attached the updated DPA (DPA_redlines_v3.pdf, v4 embedded) and the keystore matrix. Also linking the HubSpot deal for reference: https://hubspot.redwood.com/deal/DH-4721.

Thanks,
Diego
Diego Fernandez
Director, Solutions Legal Ops
Redwood Inference

Attachments: DPA_redlines_v3.pdf (PDF, 42KB - includes operator-access exhibit); keystore_control_matrix.xlsx (Excel, 14KB); sample_audit_export.csv (CSV, 8KB)
